title: Accounts Receivable
description:
Cashier Administrator

Location: Peterborough
Salary: Up to £27,000 per annum
Hours: Full-time, 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5:00pm (hybrid after 3/6 months)

The Opportunity

We are looking for a highly organised and detail-focused Cashier Administrator to join our busy finance team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with previous finance or cashiering experience who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and takes pride in maintaining accuracy.

You will play a key role in ensuring financial transactions are processed efficiently, reconciliations are completed accurately, and finance records are maintained to a high standard.

Key Responsibilities
- Posting and allocating daily cash sheets and banking transactions.
- Processing journals where required.
- Handling finance-related queries and resolving issues promptly.
- Completing full bank reconciliations and investigating discrepancies.
- Auditing cashbook supporting documentation to ensure completeness and authorisation.
- Maintaining accurate filing and record-keeping systems.
- Posting cash-paid transactions, including cheque payments and cleared banking entries.
- Supporting the wider finance team with administrative duties as required.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous experience within a finance, accounts, cashiering or administrative role.
- Strong attention to detail and high levels of accuracy.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- The ability to manage a high volume of transactions efficiently.
- Good communication skills and a proactive approach to problem-solving.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
- Experience using accounting or finance systems would be advantageous but is not essential.

Benefits
- Competitive salary up to £27,000 depending on experience.
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays.
- Contributory pension scheme.
- Life assurance.
- Ongoing training and development opportunities.
- Career progression within a growing organisation.
- Employee discounts and benefits platform.
- Friendly and supportive team environment.

Please apply for this role and send your CV to . Interviews to be held on site this week.

title: Purchase Ledger Clerk
description:
Purchase Ledger Clerk

Department: Finance / Accounts

Location: Peterborough

Salary: £27,000

About the Role

We are looking for a detail-oriented Accounts Payable Clerk to join our finance team. This role is responsible for maintaining accurate purchase ledger records, ensuring invoices and payments are processed efficiently, and supporting the smooth operation of day-to-day finance activities.

The successful candidate will have strong organisational skills, excellent attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining high levels of accuracy.

Key Responsibilities
- Maintain purchase ledger accounts and ensure records are accurate and up to date.
- Review ledgers regularly to minimise aged debt and resolve outstanding account queries.
- Download and allocate bank statements on a daily basis.
- Investigate and resolve cash allocation issues, obtaining remittances and supporting documentation where required.
- Process supplier invoices and credit notes accurately and within agreed timescales.
- Reconcile intercompany invoices and credits.
- Accurately code invoices and credit notes to the correct nominal ledger accounts.
- Complete monthly and ad hoc supplier statement reconciliations.
- Prepare and process payment runs in accordance with company procedures.
- Process ad hoc payment requests and employee expense claims, ensuring all approvals and supporting documentation are in place.
- Assist with month-end processes and reporting requirements.
- Liaise with colleagues and stakeholders to resolve invoice, payment, and account queries.

Skills & Experience
- Previous experience in an Accounts Payable, Purchase Ledger, or Finance Assistant role.
- Accountancy graduates.
- Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Good understanding of accounting processes and financial controls.
- Competent in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
- Ability to manage workload effectively and meet deadlines.
- Experience working with accounting or finance systems is desirable.

Personal Attributes
- Customer-focused approach.
- Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to identify and implement solutions.
- Proactive and organised.
- Team player willing to support colleagues when required.
- Committed to continuous improvement and delivering high standards of work.

Please send your CV to or apply for this role, interviews to be held next week.

title: Purchase Ledger Clerk
description:

Key Responsibilities:
- Monitor and manage the inbox

- Strong attention to detail and a process-driven approach

What's on Offer:
- Pay rate up to £16.50 per hour + holiday pay
- Temporary contract for an initial 6 months
- Free on site parking

This role requires the successful candidate to be office based for the first month whilst training, after which, a hybrid working arrangement can be considered with a minimum of 3 days in office per week.

If you are available at short notice and able to take on a temporary role for the next 6 months, please apply today as interviews will be taking place ASAP.

title: Purchase Ledger Controller
description:
Location: Peterborough (Hybrid Working)
Contract: Temporary, initially 12 weeks
Hours: 37 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Pay Rate: £14.07 per hour

About the Role

We are currently seeking an experienced Accounts Payable Team Member to join our finance team on an initial 12-week temporary contract.

The role is based from our Peterborough office, with hybrid working available once training has been completed and the successful candidate is fully up to speed. Initially, you will be required to work 3-4 days per week in the office, moving to 2-3 days per week following successful completion of training.

Key Responsibilities

As an Accounts Payable Team Member, you will be responsible for:
- Processing high volumes of supplier invoices accurately and efficiently.
- Reconciling supplier statements and resolving discrepancies.
- Dealing with invoice and payment queries from both internal and external stakeholders.
- Matching invoices against purchase orders, service entries and goods receipt notes.
- Ensuring all invoices are coded correctly and authorised in line with company procedures.
- Processing credits and corrections where required.
- Maintaining accurate supplier records and accounts.
- Supporting the wider finance team with ad hoc tasks as required.
- Ensuring supplier payments are processed correctly and within agreed timescales.

Skills & Experience Required

The successful candidate will have:
- Previous experience working within an Accounts Payable environment.
- A strong understanding of end-to-end Accounts Payable processes.
- Experience processing invoice credits, corrections and resolving payment queries.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Strong organisational and prioritisation skills.
- Good communication skills with the ability to liaise effectively with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- Confidence working within finance systems and Microsoft Office applications.

Desirable
- Experience of using SAP S/4 HANA would be advantageous, although this is not essential.

What We Offer
- Competitive hourly rate of £14.07 per hour.
- Hybrid working after successful completion of training.
- Opportunity to join a supportive finance team.
- Immediate start available.

If you have recent Accounts Payable experience and are looking for your next temporary opportunity, we'd love to hear from you. Please send your CV to

title: Purchasing Assistant
description:
Purchasing Assistant

Initially a 3 month contract with the possibility of moving into a maternity cover.

Hybrid Working Available

Are you looking to build a career in purchasing and procurement?

We are working with a well-established organisation that is looking to appoint a Junior Purchasing professional to join its procurement team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who has either recently started their career in purchasing or has gained some initial exposure to procurement activity and is now looking to develop their skills further.

You don't need to have extensive purchasing experience. Perhaps you have been involved in raising purchase orders, obtaining quotations, communicating with suppliers or supporting an existing procurement team and are keen to take the next step.

Working closely with internal stakeholders and external suppliers, you will help ensure goods and services are purchased efficiently, competitively and in line with business requirements.

What will you be doing
- Raising and processing purchase orders accurately.
- Requesting and comparing supplier quotations.
- Liaising with suppliers regarding orders, deliveries and queries.
- Supporting supplier research and purchasing decisions.
- Following up on outstanding orders and resolving issues.
- Maintaining accurate purchasing records and supporting internal stakeholders.

What are we looking for?

This role would suit someone who is early in their purchasing or procurement career and is keen to develop.

You may already have:
- Some experience within purchasing, procurement, buying or supply chain.
- Experience raising purchase orders or processing orders.
- Exposure to communicating with suppliers and requesting quotations.
- An understanding of basic purchasing processes.
- Strong attention to detail and good organisational skills.
- The confidence to communicate with both suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- A proactive approach and willingness to learn.

We would also consider candidates from a purchasing administration, sales administration, customer service or supply chain support background where there has been some exposure to suppliers, orders or purchasing activity.

A CIPS qualification or studying towards one would be advantageous, but is not essential.

The opportunity

This is a great opportunity to join an established procurement function and gain broader exposure to purchasing, supplier management, sourcing and procurement processes.

For the right person, the role offers the opportunity to develop commercially and professionally while building a long-term career within procurement.

If you have some initial purchasing experience and are looking for your next step, we'd be keen to hear from you.

Huntress does not discriminate on the grounds of age, race, gender, disability, creed or sexual orientation and complies with all relevant UK legislation. PLEASE NOTE! You should make yourself aware of how immigration laws apply to your situation before applying for any jobs. We are acting as a Recruitment Agency in relation to this role.

title: Medical Receptionist / Administrator
description: Abbeyview Surgery is a GP Surgery in rural Lincolnshire serving circa 9300 patients. We have a diverse, friendly team that work hard to provide the best quality care to our Practice population. Providing front of house support to patients and various administrative support to our team of clinicians, as needed from time to time. this will include some administrative duties outside of reception duties. Experience within a reception/administrative position is essential. Job summary Medical Receptionist Duties:- Greet patients and visitors in a professional and friendly manner- Answer phone calls and direct them to the appropriate department or individual- Schedule appointments and manage the appointment calendar- Check-in patients- Maintain patient records and update information as necessary- Handle incoming and outgoing emails- Ensure the waiting area is clean and organized Main duties of the job Skills:- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills- Strong organisational and multitasking abilities- Attention to detail and accuracy in data entry- Proficiency in using office equipment such as computers, printers and scanners- Ability to maintain patient confidentiality Overview of your organisation If you are a motivated individual with excellent customer service skills, we would love to hear from you. This is a great opportunity to join a dynamic team in a fast-paced medical practice.

title: Administrator
company: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust
description: OPAC Administration Services are recruiting a enthusiastic and motivated Administrators to support the Diabetes Service. The successful candidate will be providing patient focused administration support to a countywide service covering Cambridge, Fenland, Peterborough & Huntingdon liaising with our Nurses and services users to ensure an effective, efficient & streamlined service. The role will be based at our Admin hubs in Huntingdon, Cambourne, Peterborough or Doddington. We currently have 1 full time vacancy, 37.5hrs per week. Please do make contact if you would like to discuss the role further. Please note for this role you will be required to travel independently around the county meeting strict time deadlines The role involves providing comprehensive administrative support to our Diabetes Service. Responsibilities include processing referrals, managing waiting and triage lists, maintaining accurate service user records, and handling correspondence and data across multiple IT systems. The postholder will communicate professionally with referrers, clinicians, and service users, deliver an effective telephone service, coordinate interpreters, and support team operations through scanning, record management, and training of new staff. Please refer to the attached job description and person specification for full details of responsibilities Management and coordination of inbound and outbound communications and correspondence across multiple formats and channels. Responsible for the efficient coordination of appointment scheduling and proactive management of waiting lists to ensure timely access and optimal service delivery. Inputting and updating service user information and service user/team activity on computerised information systems, creating service user notes where necessary and according to policy. Maintain filing in both paper and electronic records, ensuring that it is kept up to date at all times. In accordance with Trust procedures, track and receive notes in a timely manner. Process and triage referrals across multiple pathways, applying specialist knowledge to ensure accurate prioritisation and appropriate allocation in line with service protocols. Effectively manage a high volume of incoming calls while navigating multiple systems and applying specialist knowledge to deliver a professional, responsive, and solution-focused service. Utilise both internal and external partner systems to efficiently manage workload, ensuring tasks are completed accurately, collaboratively, and in line with service standards. Handle telephone-based electronic payments and banking transactions with accuracy and security, ensuring compliance with financial procedures while delivering a professional and customer-focused service. Collect patient feedback to support continuous improvement and ensure the delivery of high-quality, patient-centred services. Manage and process incoming and outgoing mail in accordance with various established postal protocols and organisational procedures, ensuring secure and timely handling of all correspondence. Provide operational support, supervision, training, mentorship and cover to/of colleagues as directed by line manager. Providing a high level of administrative support to our clinical teams, building good professional relationships whilst setting & ensuring remit boundaries.
